react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on a dominant signal in steroid hormone metabolism. RaMP multi-database ORA (FDR 2.16e-14) and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA both rank KEGG:hsa00140 (Steroid Hormone Biosynthesis) as the top hit, with five input steroids — dehydroepiandrosterone (C01227), testosterone (C00535), androstenedione (C00280), estradiol (C00951), and dihydrotestosterone (C03917) — driving a fold-enrichment of 1250.9. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently recovers the same biology as two separate pathway hits: rank 0 'C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism' (p=0.0020, 10/10 input steroids matched) and rank 1 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' (p=0.0032, 9 matched), confirming the signal is robust to annotation source. A secondary, smaller signal emerges from mummichog for prostaglandin/thromboxane biosynthesis (rank 2, p=0.021) centred on thromboxane A2 (C02198), consistent with cross-talk between eicosanoid and steroid pathways under inflammatory or endocrine perturbation. Quinolinic acid (C03722) maps to the tryptophan-to-NAD+ pathway (Vitamin B3 metabolism, rank 4 in mummichog, p=0.053). The five driver steroids span the full androgen arm (DHEA → androstenedione → testosterone → DHT) and the aromatisation bridge to estrogens (androstenedione → estradiol), implicating coordinated disruption of CYP17A1, HSD17B, and CYP19A1 enzymatic steps.

RaMP multi-database ORA ranked SMPDB:SMP00068 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' as the top hit with FDR 2.16e-14, driven by five input steroids: dehydroepiandrosterone, androstenedione, testosterone, dihydrotestosterone (17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one), and estradiol (17β-estradiol). The same five compounds were recovered in KEGG:map00150 (identical name) and in REACT:R-HSA-196071 'Metabolism of steroid hormones' (rank 6, FDR 1.10e-13). Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently ranked MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism first (p=0.0020) with all five steroids in its matched set, and ranked MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism second (p=0.0031) with four steroids. A secondary mummichog signal emerged in MUMM:prostaglandin_formation_from_arachidonate (rank 2, p=0.0216), where thromboxane A2 (KEGG:C02198) was the sole input-matched compound. Mummichog also mapped quinolinic acid (KEGG:C03722) to MUMM:vitamin_b3_nicotinate_and_nicotinamide_metabolism (rank 4, p=0.054). The data indicate a primary disruption in androgen and estrogen metabolism centred on five C19/C18 steroids, with secondary perturbation of eicosanoid biosynthesis.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three enrichment tools returned convergent evidence for disrupted steroid hormone metabolism. RaMP multi-database ORA ranked SMPDB:SMP00068 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' as the top hit with FDR 2.16e-14, driven by five input steroids: dehydroepiandrosterone, androstenedione, testosterone, dihydrotestosterone (17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one), and estradiol (17β-estradiol). The same five compounds were recovered in KEGG:map00150 (identical name) and in REACT:R-HSA-196071 'Metabolism of steroid hormones' (rank 6, FDR 1.10e-13). Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently ranked MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism first (p=0.0020) with all five steroids in its matched set, and ranked MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism second (p=0.0031) with four steroids. A secondary mummichog signal emerged in MUMM:prostaglandin_formation_from_arachidonate (rank 2, p=0.0216), where thromboxane A2 (KEGG:C02198) was the sole input-matched compound. Mummichog also mapped quinolinic acid (KEGG:C03722) to MUMM:vitamin_b3_nicotinate_and_nicotinamide_metabolism (rank 4, p=0.054). The data indicate a primary disruption in androgen and estrogen metabolism centred on five C19/C18 steroids, with secondary perturbation of eicosanoid biosynthesis.
